mutations.because: The LAYER_DRAWERS dispatch table must register the html layer drawer so that templates with an html layer can render their backup image on the canvas rather than throwing.
mutations.retired: Retired by AR7: html left LAYER_KINDS entirely (D159's own consequence — the compositor's own comment already said an html-kind layer paints nothing, so nothing about the renderers required a distinct layer kind for it). LAYER_DRAWERS is Readonly<Record<LayerKind, LayerDrawer>>, so there is no html key left to register or drop — the type itself refuses the shape this mutation names. HL3's other mutations still cover the drawer's own behaviour where it survives.

mutations.before: `NodeCanvasCompositor: layer kind "${layer.kind}" has no drawer in this compositor — it draws image, video, shade, accent, static-text, animated-text, logo and html only`,
mutations.after: `NodeCanvasCompositor: layer kind "${layer.kind}" has no drawer in this compositor — it draws image, video, shade, accent, static-text, animated-text and logo only`,
mutations.because: The error message in drawLayer must list html among the supported layer kinds when an unknown kind is encountered, keeping diagnostic messages accurate for unsupported layers.
mutations.retired: Retired by RW-5 (L11, D131): the code is gone, not moved. This mutation shortened the kinds list in drawLayer's "no drawer" error so a template naming an unsupported kind was refused with a message that lied about what the compositor draws. `fill` was the last member of LAYER_KINDS without a drawer; L11 gave it one, LAYER_DRAWERS became a total Record, and the lookup can no longer miss for any value the type admits — so the throw, its message and the kinds list in it were all removed rather than kept as a branch no input can reach. There is no equivalent spelling to re-anchor on: what now refuses a new kind is the table's own totality, at compile time in every reader, which no text mutation can express. HL3's other mutations still cover the html drawer itself.

mutations.because: drawLogo must allow rendering when anchor is undefined if the template has an html layer, allowing canonical image-html templates with a logo to render without requiring a static-text layer.
mutations.retired: Retired by AR7: the escape hatch is gone, not moved. image-html's canonical template now requires a static-text layer exactly as image-text and video require their own text kind (D159), so 'no enabled text layer at all' is unreachable through the domain boundary for any of the three creative types — the html-kind carve-out this mutation exercised has no successor to re-anchor on. A hand-built template that still omits every text-kind layer (bypassing the boundary, as this same test file's image-text case does) throws unconditionally now, which is the behaviour HL3's own doc comment already wanted.

mutations.because: GenerateCampaignUseCase must not reject image-html creative types at the boundary guard now that the compositor has an HTML layer drawer to produce backup renditions.

The drawHtml drawer must handle button elements by rendering the rounded button background with brandColor and drawing the button text label onto the canvas. (Re-anchored by ANCHORS: X10 (#391) added the rounded clip and HL5e resolved the button's font and font size through named helpers, so the case block grew around the claim; The semantic edit is the same one; the after-text is that edit re-expressed against the current shape, not a new claim.)
mutations.retired: Retired by AR2: drawHtml returns immediately and paints no button. The html layer is raster-silent.

mutations.because: The drawHtml drawer must render image elements using the prepared background asset into the element's bounding box frame.
mutations.retired: Retired by AR2: drawHtml returns immediately and paints no image element. The html layer is raster-silent.

mutations.because: drawHtml must read its elements from the dispatched layer on the draw context — a template may carry two html layers, and hunting prepared.layers for "the" html layer paints the first list twice and never paints the second. (Re-anchored by ANCHORS: L10a wrapped the element loop in an optional layer-frame clip; The semantic edit is the same one; the after-text is that edit re-expressed against the current shape, not a new claim.)
